items.title: The type of a formal algebraic space can be checked on any one presentation
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a formal algebraic space and one of the five types -- countably indexed, countably indexed and classical, weakly adic, adic*, Noetherian -- the lemma asserts the equivalence of two formulations: that every representable etale affine formal algebraic space over it has the type, and that the members of some presentation have the type (statement lines 4681-4695). One implication is immediate; the substance is the other. Given a representable etale affine formal algebraic space over the space and a presentation, the fibre products of the given object with the members of the presentation are formal algebraic spaces, so coverings of them may be chosen, and quasi-compactness of the given object allows finitely many members of these coverings to be selected so that their coproduct covers it and is etale over it (proof lines 4697-4712). Each selected member inherits the type from the corresponding member of the presentation by the statement on affine morphisms over an affine formal algebraic space, and the finite coproduct of them does too -- a step the author marks as a small detail omitted concerning finite disjoint unions (proof lines 4712-4718). The conclusion then follows from the corresponding two-way statement for each of the five types (proof lines 4718-4729). The claim is H2: the argument combines a finite refinement by quasi-compactness with two transfers of the type, and it collects the five cases into one statement by citing the five corresponding equivalence results.
